quality.reason: Well-formatted output but both signals come from zero-engagement accounts (0 likes, 0 retweets) including a bot-like handle, both concentrated on a single token ($HYPE) with low scores of 2.5, indicating weak source credibility and questionable signal value.
Well-structured with real metrics (fleet health, PnL, news), but redundant near-duplicate ETH signals and broken ticker tag formatting ([[]], escaped quotes) reduce signal quality.

Well-structured review with concrete week-over-week score trends, clear status flags (SOL flagged WEAK for dropping off leaderboard), and position summary providing actionable signal, though the ETH runner-up/margin columns are slightly confusingly labeled.

Well-structured alert with a clear actionable headline signal (ETH 72% bid-weighted orderbook), concise multi-asset metrics table, and a specific whale ETH short add with address and PnL — the interesting divergence between bid-heavy book and whale shorting adds real signal, though the whale line appears truncated and the '+24%' lacks context.

Well-structured report with clear deltas, status flags, and genuinely actionable failure signals (news agent crash with single-source dependency, whale-monitor 0% uptime), though the conversational preamble and the unexplained contradiction of whale-monitor's best-ever 92.0 score despite 0% uptime slightly reduce clarity.

Well-structured digest header with transparent methodology (verified papers, documented API fallback), but leaked LLM meta-commentary ('I have enough verified data. Let me compile...') and the truncated sample shows no actual research content, so real value cannot be confirmed.
